newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand intervenes to stall baht slide.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand intervenes to stall baht slide.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Thursday intervened in the spot baht/dollar market to curb any baht sell-off against the dollar, especially after rumours about the financial health of a major Thai finance company, dealers said.
After the intervention, believed by dealers to have been made in foreign markets, the baht recovered to 25.900-25.905 to the dollar after sliding to a level as low as 25.925, dealers said.

"The Bank of Thailand sold a large amount of the dollars at the rate of about 25.912-25.913. The baht selloff this morning was partly triggered by rumours about Finance One," said one senior dealer at a local bank.

Finance One, Thailand's leading finance company, has denied stock market rumours that it may not be able to meet its debt obligations. It said its ability to meet payments for its bonds and foreign exchange position were sound.
Another dealer at Bank of Asia said the intervention was believed to have taken place in offshore spot markets.
"The intervention was made in offshore markets. Many here were unaware about the intervention," she said.
The Finance One rumour sparked a sharp fall in most share prices on Wednesday and also led to some speculative ditching of the baht for the bullish dollar, dealers said.
"The intervention significantly helped the baht from selling pressure. It also made offshore players more cautious about attacking the baht," said another dealer at a European bank.
